chapter: Hollywood, Ken Murray and the Penguin years
title: Ed Snead, George Duvivier and a 1945 photograph
summary: Snead's Lunceford connection, Duvivier's session, and a Queens Terrace photo.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: That's right, because Snead--I'm pretty sure Snead was the last bass player that Jimmy Lunceford had. Jimmy Lunceford died in '47, so it would have to be '48.
I didn't know he played for Jimmy Lunceford.
Yeah, he did. He came up and took George Duvivier's place.
He did?
Yeah.
George Duvivier made that record with me.
Which one?
Blue Memories.
On Penguin?
Yeah.
He wasn't working with you thought; was he?
Yeah, he made a few dates.
He's the number one man in New York as far as I'm concerned. Where is this, and how late is this? Oh, this is back at the Queens Terrace.
Doesn't that have a date on it?
There's nothing on here but the names. Fauntleroy; he's still around, isn't he?
Yeah, he's around.
Fauntleroy, George Spots, this one I can't quite see.
That's Abie Baker.
That's Abie Baker; yeah. This is Kenny?
Right.
This can't be too late then, unless he worked with you more than once; did he work with you more than once?
No.

Then this has got to be '45 or '46. Yeah, this has to be the same time as this other picture. This is back at the Queens Terrace; this is 1945. So in other words, Spots probably took Buji Ward's place. What happened to Buji, is he still around?
I don't know.
